sc: School child, recurrent wheeze, night cough, wheeze on running, eczema → Asthma: spirometry
Asthmatic child, drowsy, silent chest, SpO2 < 92% → Life-threatening attack: PICU
Asthmatic on ICS with white plaques in the mouth → Oral thrush: spacer + rinse
f: Recurrent wheeze, cough at night and with exercise, chest tightness · triggers: colds, dust, smoke, cold air
Spirometry: FEV1 rise ≥ 12% after salbutamol · FEV1/FVC < 0.9 · possible from 5–6 years
Reliever salbutamol · controller inhaled corticosteroid · step up: LABA, montelukast · step down after 3 months of control
< 4 yr: MDI + spacer + face mask · older: spacer + mouthpiece · always check technique and adherence first
Oxygen (SpO2 94–98%) · salbutamol + ipratropium · prednisolone 1–2 mg/kg 3–5 days · severe: IV MgSO4 40 mg/kg (max 2 g)
Life-threatening: silent chest, cyanosis, drowsy, SpO2 < 92% · normal or rising PaCO2 = tiring
trap: A normal chest between attacks does not exclude asthma · clubbing is not asthma (think CF) · a silent chest is danger, not improvement
